verdict.rationale: Pydantic AI documents agents that run on a durable background queue, and durable execution that survives failures and restarts for long-running, asynchronous workflows. That is a first-party basis for autonomous background runs. However, the evidence shows no built-in way to set up automations: no scheduling, triggers, or recurring jobs, so a developer must wire up invocation themselves. Missing for 10: recurring schedule or trigger configuration, a documented automation setup flow, hands-on corroboration of background autonomous runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: The same agent runs everywhere you need it: behind a web frontend, in the terminal, on a voice call, on a durable background queue
handle long-running, asynchronous, and human-in-the-loop workflows with production-grade reliability
Build typed agents, long-running coding and research agents
